## How to accept

### Individual contributors

You do not need to sign anything in advance. When you open your first pull request against `averemee-si/oracdc`, the CLA Assistant bot comments on it and asks you to accept.
If you agree to the Agreement above, post the following text as a **new comment** in the pull request, exactly as written:

```
I have read the oracdc Contributor License Agreement and I hereby sign the CLA
```

The bot records your GitHub username, GitHub user id, the pull request number and a timestamp in the signature ledger (see [Records](#records)) and sets the `CLA` check to passing. You do this once, later pull requests are matched against the ledger automatically.

If the check does not update after you comment, post `recheck` as another comment.

### Contributing on behalf of an employer

If your employer owns the intellectual property in the work you contribute, which is usually the case when you contribute during working hours, with employer equipment, or within your field of employment, a comment from your personal GitHub account is not sufficient on its own. Your employer must accept this Agreement through a person authorised to bind it.

Use the [Corporate Contributor License Agreement](CORPORATE-CLA.md). Your company signs it once and lists in Schedule A the people authorised to contribute on its behalf. Email **oracle@a2.solutions** for the signature copy, or send the completed agreement there directly.

Once the corporate agreement is in place, the listed GitHub usernames are added to the automated check's `allowlist` and the bot no longer asks them to accept individually. Schedule A can be updated by email whenever the team changes.

### Contributions that are not your own work

Code copied from another project, generated from a third-party source, or otherwise not authored by you cannot be accepted under this Agreement. If your pull request contains third-party material, say so explicitly in the pull request description and name the upstream project and its license, so that it can be reviewed separately.

## Records

Acceptances for version 1.0 of this Agreement are stored as JSON in `signatures/version1/cla.json` on the `cla-signatures` branch of this repository. The git history of that file is the record of who accepted, and when.

Pull requests are locked after they are merged, so that a signing comment cannot be removed after the fact.

## Versioning

The Agreement text is versioned. If it changes, the new text is published as version 2.0 of this document, the workflow is pointed at a new ledger (`signatures/version2/cla.json`), and all contributors are asked to accept again on their next pull request. Acceptance of one version is never silently carried over to another.

Contributions accepted under an earlier version remain licensed under the version that was in force when they were contributed.
